newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies end up, but early gains fade.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies end up, but early gains fade.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mostly higher, but upside momentum waned after prices got an initial lift from a sharp rise in Japan's 20-day June trade surplus.
Yen futures ended firmer but drifted down through the session after a burst of activity sent dollar/yen diving to 111.98 overnight, IMM traders said.
Japan's Finance Ministry said the trade surplus in the first 20 days of June soared 129.3 percent year-on-year. Current account data for May will be released Tuesday.
Mark futures also gave back early gains and finished near the session low but did not break the contract low of $0.5721 set Thursday.
Traders said futures got an early boost from comments by Bavarian officials that rekindled fears of a delayed start to European monetary union.

Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber was quoted by the Financial Times as saying a slow start to EMU was better than a weak single currency. And Erwin Huber, the Bavarian finance minister, said EMU could begin without France.
Mark futures fell back toward unchanged levels after French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said France remained committed to a timely EMU launch.
British pound futures began the session on a weak note after a slump in May manufacturing output dampened prospects for a rate increase at this week's Bank of England policy meeting, traders said.

Manufacturing output in Britain fell 1.1 percent in May, compared with expectations for a 0.2 percent rise, and industrial production as a whole declined 0.9 percent versus a forecast rise of 0.2 percent.

However, sterling rebounded to close slightly higher, with most analysts still anticipating a rate hike announcement after the new Monetary Policy Committee ends its meeting Thursday. Official British interest rates now stand at 6.5 percent.
In sterling options, one trading firm late in the session bought 2,000 September straddles and 4,000 December straddles, all in the $1.6400 strike.
Traders said the market's main focus this week is U.S. June producer price data set for release Friday. PPI is forecast unchanged and the core rate up 0.1 percent.
Mexican peso futures were buoyant in good volume following opposition victories in Sunday's midterm elections, floor traders said.
Australian dollar futures ended lower in light volume, under pressure from last week's announcement that the central bank sold 167 tonnes of gold this year.

September yen ended up $0.000060 at $0.008956, marks ended up $0.0002 at $0.5740, Swiss francs rose $0.0036 at $0.6907, sterling was up $0.0002 at $1.6874, Canadian dollars were down $0.0026 at $0.7294, Australian dollars were down $0.0096 at $0.7446 and Mexican pesos rose $0.000725 to $0.122900.
